title: ADR-0032 — API Protocol Selection Matrix Rules
description: Machine-readable rules encoding ADR-0032 Protocol Selection Matrix. Mandatory protocol selection for internal, external, and BFF communication.
adrTitle: API Protocol Selection Matrix (REST vs gRPC vs GraphQL)

rules.title: Internal service-to-service uses gRPC
rules.description: MANDATE: gRPC (Protocol Buffers over HTTP/2) for all internal service-to-service communication between bounded contexts. Scope: synchronous calls where both services are owned by the organization.
rules.rationale: ADR-0032 §Decision: High performance, binary serialization, and strict type-safety through unified .proto contracts.
rules.validationQuery: Internal service calls use gRPC. No REST calls between internal bounded contexts (telemetry confirms).

rules.title: Public and external APIs use REST
rules.description: MANDATE: REST (JSON over HTTPS) for all public third-party and external integration. Scope: external customer integrations, legacy corporate gateway connections, and global developer public APIs.
rules.rationale: ADR-0032 §Decision: Industry universality, trivial consumption, easiest debugging/testing, broad interactive documentation.
rules.validationQuery: Public API endpoints use REST/JSON. OpenAPI spec available for all public APIs.

rules.title: BFF uses REST primary, GraphQL targeted
rules.description: Default to REST for standard flows (CRUD commands). Adopt GraphQL strictly at the NestJS BFF level ONLY when a screen requires complex data aggregation (fetching Entities, associated Taxonomies, Audits, and relations simultaneously).
rules.rationale: ADR-0032 §Decision: Prevents mobile/web over-fetching and multiple sequential roundtrips for rich read scenarios.
rules.validationQuery: BFF uses REST for standard CRUD. GraphQL used only for aggregate read scenarios with documented justification.

rules.title: GraphQL resolvers never in domain layer
rules.description: GraphQL runtime logic MUST exist only within Tier-2 BFF application nodes. Core domain API definitions never natively support GraphQL resolvers. This prevents view-specific constraints from leaking into domain business logic.
rules.rationale: ADR-0032 §Architecture Guidelines: GraphQL isolation. Core domain must remain protocol-agnostic.
rules.validationQuery: No GraphQL resolvers in Core or Application layers. GraphQL exists only in BFF/Api layer.

rules.title: Proto files centralized in Contracts library
rules.description: All internal gRPC service schemas (.proto) are hosted and versioned in a unified Contracts library (libs/contracts or similar) to prevent drifted interface models.
rules.rationale: ADR-0032 §Architecture Guidelines: Protobuf centralization prevents interface drift between services.
rules.validationQuery: .proto files exist in shared Contracts library. No duplicate .proto definitions across services.

rules.title: File uploads/streams prefer gRPC streaming
rules.description: File uploads and streaming scenarios SHOULD use gRPC streaming capabilities for native streaming or REST multipart as fallback.
rules.rationale: ADR-0032 §Selection Decision Tree: Native streaming capability or simple multipart.
rules.validationQuery: Streaming endpoints evaluated for gRPC first, REST multipart as fallback.

rules.title: Breaking changes require version bump
rules.description: Breaking changes to inter-service contracts (gRPC .proto or REST OpenAPI) require a new major version. Consumer-driven contract tests must pass before merge.
rules.rationale: ADR-0032 §Decision: Contract versioning ensures backward compatibility during service evolution.
rules.validationQuery: Contract tests enforce backward compatibility. Breaking changes blocked by CI.

protocolMatrix.justification: Low latency, binary compaction, strongly typed

exitCriteria.description: All inter-service communication uses correct protocol per matrix. Contracts centralized and versioned.
